content_of_post_to_comment:
Deleted Facebook in 2018 after I got married because I started to not care what everyone from high school was up to. Then I deleted Twitter shortly after because I got bored with doomscrolling. Then a year later Instagram's popular feed showed me some really disgusting image after I checked out an influencer mom's profile. I reported the disgusting image and it wasn't removed because it didn't violate Instagram's TOS despite being literal illegal content. I deleted my account and never looked back.

The only social media I use these days is LinkedIn (which I barely go on) and Pinterest because I'm renovating my house. I do use other sites like YouTube, Storygraph, Letterboxd, but I don't spend hours a day on them.

My biggest gripe is Reddit. I can't seem to quit the damn site. My husband says he will never get off it because that's where we met and he loves doomscrolling on r/popular. It's the only social media he uses. It's become so bad. Can't share my hatred for AI without being accused of being a bot myself. People bullying others in comment sections. I reported a subreddit for being hate speech and Reddit gave me a warning when I described the sub to someone in a comment. All I did was ask for help on how to report the sub. Why Reddit still allows it is beyond me.

I've just recently joined a WhatsApp group with random people I've met off a subreddit and we are going to meet up for the first time on Saturday. I moved abroad 10 years ago and have struggled to make friends so this seems like a good opportunity for me. I just struggle to leave Reddit for good. I mean, to be honest someone threatened my life when I said AI wastes water so I deleted my acct to start over. Why couldn't I just be done for good? I have enough hobbies outside my computer like sewing, wild swimming, journaling, biking, cooking, baking, etc.

I just want to get off here, but I'm always pulled back in and my husband loves to send me posts every day.
